AfterCombatVictory.maps_to: after_combat_end (sts2_rl/relics/sword_of_stone.py), the run-level PLAIN pass dispatched at sts2_rl/run.py:1380-1381 after the after_combat_end_early pass
AfterCombatVictory.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the AfterCombatVictoryEarly / AfterCombatVictory two-pass dispatch is real. On the combat side, HookSystem._each walks the phases very_early -> early -> plain -> late as COMPLETE separate passes whenever any listener declares a phase variant (sts2_rl/hooks.py:36, 153-180); on the run side RunState.finish_combat runs `after_combat_end_early` over every relic and only then `after_combat_end` (sts2_rl/run.py:1371-1381). Both mirror Hook.AfterCombatVictory (Hook.cs:340-352). The elite gate, the counter, the threshold and the in-place replacement were already faithful; the two-pass distinction was the rollup's only gap.

guards.what: N1 (SWEEP-A CANDIDATE, SETTLED AS FAITHFUL): `elites_defeated` is never reset -- and it must not be, because C#'s ElitesDefeated is a [SavedProperty]
guards.rationale: This is the unit the batch-15 brief pre-diagnosed as 'Sweep A candidate (elites_defeated; C# resets at AfterCombatVictory)', and the second half of that description is WRONG -- AfterCombatVictory does not reset the field, it INCREMENTS it (SwordOfStone.cs:44). Settled on the merits per PROMPT.md v6 item 1 (a sweep may escalate a candidate, never clear one -- and, symmetrically, a candidate is not a finding). The field is `[SavedProperty] public int ElitesDefeated` (SwordOfStone.cs:25-38), i.e. serialised into the run save and therefore per-RUN by design, exactly like the nunchaku counter .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md discusses; the sim's per-instance counter on a relic that lives on RunState.relics for the whole run reproduces that. The FIXED sweep agrees: re-running `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-reset` for this batch prints `sword_of_stone ['elites_defeated'] / written by: elites_defeated<-['__init__', 'after_combat_end'] / C# resets: NONE (may be per-run by design)` -- the brief's 'resets at AfterCombatVictory' wording is the OLD, defect-3 output (an override census printed as a reset census), which the rewritten column no longer emits. EXECUTED end to end (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b15.py b15-swords): five successive ELITE victories on ONE relic instance carry the counter 1,2,3,4,5 and the relic list flips to ['sword_of_jade'] on the fifth; a MONSTER-room victory leaves the counter at 0. PROMPT.md bug class 13's required trace therefore ends in 'no reset is correct', not 'a reset is missing'.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): AfterCombatVictory is TWO separate C# passes (AfterCombatVictoryEarly then AfterCombatVictory) and the sim has one after_combat_end walk which also stands in for Hook.AfterCombatEnd
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the AfterCombatVictoryEarly / AfterCombatVictory two-pass dispatch is real. On the combat side, HookSystem._each walks the phases very_early -> early -> plain -> late as COMPLETE separate passes whenever any listener declares a phase variant (sts2_rl/hooks.py:36, 153-180); on the run side RunState.finish_combat runs `after_combat_end_early` over every relic and only then `after_combat_end` (sts2_rl/run.py:1371-1381). Both mirror Hook.AfterCombatVictory (Hook.cs:340-352). Sword of Stone implements the PLAIN pass (SwordOfStone.cs:40) and is now guaranteed to run after every Early listener. WAS: one flat after_combat_end walk in relic-list order. NOTE, unchanged and still open elsewhere: C# also distinguishes Hook.AfterCombatEnd from Hook.AfterCombatVictory and the sim folds both onto after_combat_end; that collapse is audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json G10's, and it is harmless at this site because run.py:1371's `not self.is_dead` gate makes the sim's dispatch victory-only.

guards.what: N2: `RelicCmd.Replace(this, SwordOfJade)` (SwordOfStone.cs:48) vs the port's hand-rolled in-place swap (sword_of_stone.py:38-42)
guards.rationale: Read against the command rather than assumed. RelicCmd.Replace (RelicCmd.cs:74-82) is `indexOfOriginal = Relics.IndexOf(original); Remove(original); Obtain(replace, player, indexOfOriginal)`. The port does the index lookup and the in-place assignment (`run.relics[run.relics.index(self)] = jade`) and then calls `jade.after_obtained(run)`. Everything Remove/Obtain add on top is either a no-op here or presentation: Remove fires `relic.AfterRemoved()` (RelicCmd.cs:65) and SwordOfStone overrides no AfterRemoved; Obtain's `player.RelicGrabBag.Remove(relic)` / `SharedRelicGrabBag.Remove(relic)` (RelicCmd.cs:41-45) cannot matter because Sword of Jade is EVENT rarity and is absent from the transcribed bag (executed b15-pool), so there is nothing to remove; `FloorAddedToDeck` (RelicCmd.cs:52) has no sim counterpart and no reader in either the sim or, for this relic, in C#; the history entry, the animation and MarkRelicAsSeen are presentation/meta-progression. AfterObtained is dispatched on both sides and is a no-op on both (relic/sword_of_jade N4). EXECUTED (b15-swords): the swap lands at the same list index. Rule 7: RelicCmd.cs, run.py and relics/sword_of_jade.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: `room.RoomType == RoomType.Elite` (SwordOfStone.cs:42), `ElitesDefeated >= DynamicVars['Elites'].BaseValue` (:46), and the increment-before-test order
guards.rationale: DynamicVar('Elites', 5m) (SwordOfStone.cs:23) with no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so ELITES = 5 (sword_of_stone.py:23) is the pinned non-ascension value, and the port's `>=` matches C#'s `>=` rather than `==` (which matters only if a counter could ever skip 5). The increment precedes the test on both sides, so the fifth elite is the one that transforms -- EXECUTED (b15-swords): the flip happens on elite 5, not 6. The room gate matches: the sim's RoomType.ELITE is the room type RunState.finish_combat is called with, and a MONSTER room leaves the counter untouched (executed). Boss rooms are RoomType.Boss on both sides and correctly do not count.

guards.what: N4: C# replaces the relic while the combat is still ENDING; the sim replaces it after finish_combat
guards.rationale: Checked because a mid-teardown relic swap is where a hook-lifetime bug would hide. C# fires Hook.AfterCombatVictory from EndCombatInternal (audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json G10 cites CombatManager.cs:970-1033), so RelicCmd.Obtain runs while the CombatState still exists and the new relic is NOT registered as a combat listener (the listener list is rebuilt per combat from player.Relics). The sim's after_combat_end is dispatched from RunState.finish_combat (run.py:1205-1207), strictly after the combat object is done being read, and the new relic is attached to the NEXT CombatState by relic.attach (relics/base.py:152-155). Both therefore give Sword of Jade its first hook in the following combat, which is also where its own AfterRoomEntered/on_combat_start effect belongs. The one C# subtlety with no consequence here: mutating player.Relics during a listener pass is safe because Hook re-enumerates, and the sim's dispatch iterates `list(self.relics)` (run.py:1206), a copy -- so neither side skips or double-visits a relic because of the swap.

guards.what: N5: no undo_after_obtained, and no IsAllowed override
guards.rationale: The ABSENCE of undo_after_obtained is faithful per PROMPT.md v6 item 3 -- the helper has no C# counterpart. It is also genuinely unnecessary here: the pickup mutates nothing outside run.relics (there is no AfterObtained at all), so a conformance relic swap needs no unwinding. SwordOfStone.cs declares no IsAllowed / IsAllowedAtNeow override, so the relic is not in sweep B's 17-relic IsBeforeAct3TreasureChest cluster and the base True for is_allowed_at_neow (relics/base.py:159) is consistent with RelicModel.IsAllowedAtNeow delegating to IsAllowed (RelicModel.cs:443-446; PROMPT.md v6 item 2). Event rarity keeps it out of Neow's pools in practice anyway.
